chunks.text: 31-year-old female, Unemployed, resident of Bishan, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few questions to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with an LMA. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You've been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, and Obesity. Can you tell me a bit about how these are managed, and if you've had any recent changes or issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My diabetes is controlled with Metformin, 500mg twice daily. Blood sugar levels have been okay, not too high or low. My blood pressure is managed with Lisinopril, 10mg once daily. I also take Atorvastatin for cholesterol and Citalopram, but I stopped that one already as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that. I see in your records that you have no known allergies. But just to be thorough, can you please confirm if you have any allergies, particularly to Latex, which might not be documented?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, actually, I think I am allergic to Latex. I remember once during a check-up, they used Latex gloves, and my hand got really itchy and red. I didn't think much of it then, but maybe it's important to mention now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's very important for us to know. We'll make sure to note that and take all necessary precautions. Are you currently on any other medications or supplements besides what you've mentioned?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, that's all. I stopped Citalopram as per the instructions, and I haven't taken anything else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never had surgery before, so I'm a bit nervous.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: It's completely normal to feel that way. We're here to make sure everything goes smoothly. Can you tell me about your NPO status? When was the last time you had food or drink?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a light dinner last night around 7 PM and a sip of water this morning around 6 AM. Nothing else since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect, that's within the guidelines. Lastly, how would you describe your overall functional status? Are you able to walk, climb stairs, or do other daily activities without much difficulty?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, I can walk and do my daily stuff, but sometimes I get a bit tired because of my weight. But I manage okay lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It helps us understand your baseline. We'll make sure to support you throughout the process. Is there anything else you'd like to ask or share before we proceed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You're very welcome. We're here to ensure your safety and comfort. I'll be with you every step of the way. We'll get started soon, and I'll make sure you're fully prepared before going into the operating room.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA size four in place, secure airway

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] fentanyl twenty micrograms IV for analgesia

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] vecuronium fifty milligrams IV for muscle relaxation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] normal saline one liter IV fluid running at one hundred fifty mL per hour

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] hypotension noted, mean arterial pressure forty five mmHg, atropine one milligram IV administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:15] surgery completed, emergence started with neostigmine two milligrams and sugammadex one hundred sixty milligrams IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, but I have some pain in my tummy and my back is aching a bit.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate the pain?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5. It's not too bad, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Have you felt nauseous or had any vomiting since the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I haven't thrown up, but I feel a little bit sick in my stomach.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Are you comfortable with your breathing? Any shortness of breath or throat discomfort from the LMA?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, but my throat feels a bit sore. Like I have a slight cough.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operating room or waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really, I was out cold. But I do remember waking up here in the recovery area.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You have a history of diabetes and high blood pressure. Have you noticed any dizziness, sweating, or other symptoms that might suggest low blood sugar or high blood pressure?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No dizziness or anything like that. I feel a bit tired, but that's probably normal after surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we'll keep an eye on your vitals and blood sugar levels. Let the nurse know if the pain or nausea gets worse.
